coverage_failures.evidence_item: ActionDeadCode (coreaction.cc:3697 pushConsumed, :3717 propagateConsumed, :4070-4208 apply) does THREE things in one Action: (a) consume-bit dataflow propagation = value facts; (b) dead op destruction = op-graph mutation; (c) is gated by deadRemovalAllowed/deadcodedelay = SSA/heritage coupling.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: A: consume bits are an S5 'Value & Type Facts' artifact, dead-op removal is an S3 'Op-Graph' mutation, and the deadcodedelay gate is an S3 SSA-construction substage feedback (edge S3->S3). One file, three of A's stages, and A never tells the developer where ActionDeadCode 'lives'. B: same split across S2 (deadcode gate substage), S4 (value-propagation/dead-elim substage), and the consume-bit fact has no home (B has no value-fact artifact distinct from S5 type lattice). C: splits across S4 (Dataflow Simplification dead-elim substage), S3 (deadcode delay substage), with consume bits homeless. The user explicitly named this as a hard case and NO proposal gives ActionDeadCode a single home.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Make the unit-of-placement a (file, Action) pair mapped to its DOMINANT owned artifact, and represent the secondary effects as explicit feedback edges from that home. ActionDeadCode's home is the op-graph stage (it owns op destruction); its consume-bit computation is an internal analysis feeding the value-fact substage, and its deadcodedelay gate is an inbound edge from SSA construction. Document multi-artifact Actions in a 'straddler registry' so a developer/agent is never told an Action is in exactly one place when it is not.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: jumptable.cc: recoverAddresses (:2636, called during flow generation/frontend) vs matchModel (:2696) + setRestartPending (:2716) + recoverLabels (:2727, called post-simplification). The jump table is recovered in two temporally separated phases in different pipeline bands.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: A places the whole jump table as a sub-artifact of S3 (Op-Graph & CFG) with a substage 'flow completion / jump-table recovery', but the FIRST recovery happens during S2 'Instruction & Context Stream' flow following (before the CFG even exists - report 01: 'block generation is lazy'), and the matchModel restart fires from the simplification fixed point. So in A the jumptable substage sits in S3 yet its trigger lives in S2 and its rollback in S5. B folds it entirely into S1 'Reachable-Code Graph' which is defensible but then cannot represent the post-SSA matchModel restart cleanly. C is the only one that gets close (S1->S1 'reduced-pipeline sub-query' edge for stageJumpTable) but still puts jump-table recovery wholly in S1 while matchModel demonstrably runs after simplification (jumptable.cc recoverLabels is invoked late).
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Model the jump table as a first-class cross-stage artifact (like Ghidra's jumpvec member, funcdata.hh:90) with TWO substages bound to TWO stages: 'partial table recovery' in the flow/decode stage and 'label/model match' in the dataflow-simplification stage, joined by an explicit persisted-hint restart edge (Override.insertMultistageJump). This is the clearest case where keying by 'owned artifact' alone fails: the artifact is owned across stages and the taxonomy must allow an artifact to have substages in more than one stage.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: A fuses value facts (nonzero/consume/value-set ranges) and the type lattice into ONE stage S5 'Value & Type Facts'.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: For navigation this collapses two distinct LLM intervention targets. A 'wrong range -> missed switch bound' symptom (ValueSetSolver, rangeutil) and a 'wrong type' symptom (Typehoon/ActionInferTypes) both resolve to S5, but their assertion types and re-run scopes differ sharply: value-set facts feed S3 jump-table bounds (OptionJumpTableMax) and determined-branch removal, while type facts feed S6 variable layout and S8 casts. An agent told 'go to S5' cannot tell which substage of S5 owns its symptom without re-deriving the split A erased.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Keep S5 as one stage (the co-iteration evidence justifies it for Ghidra) but make the THREE substages A already lists (constant/pointer interp; lattice propagation; aggregate reconstruction) carry distinct downstream-edge sets and assertion types, and explicitly note that value-set/range facts are a fourth substage feeding S3 (not just S6/S8). Borrow B's per-substage assertion catalog so the fused stage is still navigable.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: B asserts SEVEN feedback mechanism types (adds (f) worklist-re-enqueue and (g) lazy-dirty recompute) and places S2/S3/S4 as three separate stages using angr's finer ClinicStage grain even though Reko fuses register-SSA + stack-SSA + expression-building into one DataFlowAnalysis stage with ~15 transforms (report 09).
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: For kuna (a Ghidra extraction) the finer angr grain is a forced placement: Ghidra has NO stage boundary between its SSA web (S2) and its call/prototype model (S3) - ActionHeritage, ActionActiveParam, ActionInferTypes all live INSIDE one mainloop fixed point (coreaction.cc:5636-5824, report 00). A developer trying to locate ActionActiveParam in kuna source finds it interleaved with heritage in the same ActionGroup; B's three-stage split (S2 Definition Web / S3 Call Model / S4 Variable Model as separate ordered stages) does not correspond to any boundary in the code kuna actually contains. B even concedes this in its H4 critique (angr two-level SSA, Reko under-segmentation) but ships the split anyway.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: For the kuna-targeted taxonomy, set stage boundaries at GHIDRA's group/root-action boundaries (the artifact each owns), not angr's ClinicStage indices, and treat the angr/Reko finer or coarser grains as substage annotations. The SSA web, call specs, and value/type facts co-iterate in Ghidra's mainloop and should be one 'fixed-point band' with named substages, not three sequential stages - otherwise kuna developers cannot find the boundary B names.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: C lists S0 'Assertion Store' as a numbered stage in the ordered list (S0..S9) AND simultaneously says it is 'not a processing stage in the first-pass sense'.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: This contradicts the user's definition that stages 'trigger linearly on the FIRST pass'. The assertion store is read at the top of EVERY stage on every run (reports 00/03/07/08 all confirm: Override + Symbol DB, KB, Program.User are consulted by each stage), so giving it an ordinal position implies a first-pass trigger order it does not have. A developer asked 'what runs after S0' gets a wrong mental model. A handles this correctly by calling it an 'orthogonal plane (S0)'; C should too.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Adopt A's framing: the assertion/knowledge store is an orthogonal plane, not an ordinal stage. Remove it from the S0..S9 linear sequence and depict it as a column that every stage reads on (re-)entry and some stages write back to (ActionOutputPrototype, CompleteCallingConventions, CallRewriter.EnsureSignature).

coverage_failures.evidence_item: C splits S6 Type Reconstruction and notes Ghidra 'fuses S5 type inference INTO the S3 mainloop' but still presents S3 SSA, S4 Dataflow, S5 Variables, S6 Types as four sequential first-pass stages.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: In Ghidra ActionInferTypes (S6), ActionRestructureVarnode (S5), oppool1 simplification (S4), and ActionHeritage (S3) are all members of the SAME mainloop ActionGroup that repeats to quiescence (coreaction.cc:5636-5824). There is no first-pass linear order S3->S4->S5->S6; they are a mutual fixed point. C's own hypothesis critique admits 'the first-pass linear ORDER of S4/S5/S6 is partly a fiction for Ghidra' - so the proposal ships a stage order it knows is fictional for the very decompiler kuna extracts.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Collapse C's S3/S4/S5/S6 into a single 'mutual fixed-point band' stage for the kuna model, with SSA-web / simplified-ops / variable-model / type-lattice as four co-resident artifacts and substages, and represent the Ghidra-vs-angr/Reko scheduling difference (interleaved vs post-stabilization solver) as a documented substage property, exactly as C's own cross-cutting finding recommends.

cross_proposal_assessment: All three converge on the load-bearing truths (artifact-keyed stages per H4; orthogonal durable-assertion store per H3; non-linearity via typed feedback edges) and all three independently arrive at ~8-9 stages, which is the right grain - the 19-stage list's failure (forcing Dataflow/Memory/AggregateTypes/Interproc into module-less buckets) does not recur in any of them. Source confirms the central artifact split they all rely on: funcdata.hh:90/94/95 physically stores jumpvec, bblocks, and sblocks as three separate members, so 'CFG' and 'structured region tree' really are distinct artifacts with distinct invalidation stories. PROPOSAL A is the best fit for the kuna use case as the STAGE SKELETON: it is the most faithful to Ghidra's actual data structures (it is the only one that correctly demotes SSA to a reversible PROPERTY of the op-graph rather than a stage - vindicated by Reko's UnSsaTransform and Ghidra's in-place MULTIEQUAL insertion - and the only one that treats the assertion store purely as an orthogonal plane), and its feedback edges map cleanly onto setRestartPending + Override. PROPOSAL B is the best for the AGENT-NAVIGATION layer: its decision-family clustering with a named assertion type per substage, HARD-vs-HINT lock strength, and especially its flagging of ~30% LATENT (no-override) decision points is exactly the catalog an LLM agent needs and is the single most actionable artifact for kuna's product roadmap. PROPOSAL C is the best for the SCHEDULING/RE-RUN-SCOPE model: it is the only one that makes 'reduced-pipeline sub-query' (Ghidra stageJumpTable cloning a partial Funcdata and switching to the 11-group jumptable pipeline) and 'rewind scope (op/block/region/function/program)' first-class, which is precisely what kuna must instrument to beat upstream Ghidra's blunt clearAnalysis + maxrestarts=1. Graft into A: from B, the per-substage (assertion-type, lock-strength, LATENT?) catalog and the admission-policy/confidence-graded HINT concept; from C, the rewind-scope attribute on every feedback edge, the named-reduced-pipeline variants as first-class objects, and the 'what survives a rewind' (survivability) axis that grounds H3. A's mechanism set (H1 a-e) is sufficient if augmented with C's restart-vs-subquery distinction and B's worklist-re-enqueue/lazy-dirty as edge ANNOTATIONS rather than promoting them to new stage-level mechanism types.
forced_placements: A and C both force the jump table into a single stage (A: S3 sub-artifact; C: S1) even though jumptable.cc proves recovery is split between flow-following (recoverAddresses, :2636, before any CFG exists) and post-simplification (matchModel/recoverLabels, :2696/:2727). The artifact is owned across two stages; forcing it into one is the same error the old taxonomy made with cross-cutting concerns.

B forces a three-way stage split (S2 SSA web / S3 Call model / S4 Variable model) using angr's ClinicStage grain onto kuna, but Ghidra interleaves ActionHeritage + ActionActiveParam + ActionInferTypes + Merge inside ONE mainloop ActionGroup (coreaction.cc:5636-5824). For the Ghidra-extraction target there is no code boundary at B's S2/S3/S4 cuts - a developer cannot point to the file/line where S2 ends and S3 begins.
C forces S0 (assertion store) into the ordinal first-pass sequence S0..S9 while admitting it is not a processing stage; this puts a non-triggering plane into a triggering order.
C forces S3 Op-Graph / S4 Dataflow / S5 Variables / S6 Types into a sequential first-pass order that C itself labels 'partly a fiction for Ghidra' - the mutual fixed point has no linear order.

A forces value-set/range facts into S5 alongside the type lattice; but ranges primarily feed S3 (jump-table bounds via OptionJumpTableMax, determined-branch removal at coreaction.cc:537) not S6/S8, so an agent debugging a 'missed switch case due to wrong bound' is sent to the type stage when the relevant computation (ValueSetSolver, rangeutil) feeds the flow/CFG stage. This is a softer version of the old taxonomy's 'Range' module having no real owner.

A and C place ActionMarkExplicit/Implied (explicit-vs-implied) in the variable stage (A S6, C S5), but report 03 says it does NOT interact with user intervention and is purely an output-readability decision consulted at emission; it sits awkwardly between the variable artifact and the text artifact, and neither proposal flags that the only override is global (angr expr_collapse_depth) with Ghidra having no per-variable knob - a LATENT surface B would have flagged but A/C bury.
synthesis_recommendation:
Adopt PROPOSAL A's stage skeleton as the spine, restructured into bands to honor Ghidra's fixed-point reality, then overlay B's per-substage assertion catalog and C's scheduling attributes. Concrete recommendation:

STAGE LIST (artifact-keyed, with an orthogonal plane - NOT an ordinal stage):
- PLANE P0 Assertion/Knowledge Store (orthogonal; read by every stage on (re-)run, written back by prototype-output/CC actions). Maps to Ghidra Symbol DB + Override + FuncProto locks. This is A's S0 framing; reject C's ordinal placement.
- S1 Image & Symbol Map (A.S1) - bytes, segment map, code/data/pointer partition.
- S2 Instruction & Context Stream (A.S2) - decoded ops + visited map + context bits, pre-CFG (block gen is lazy, report 01).
- S3 Op-Graph & CFG (A.S3) - the mutable op web + bblocks (funcdata.hh:94). SSA is a REVERSIBLE PROPERTY substage here, not a stage (keep A's strongest single insight). Jump table is a CROSS-STAGE artifact with a substage here AND in S2 (recoverAddresses) joined by a persisted-hint restart edge.
- BAND B1 'Mutual Fixed-Point' = {SSA-web, simplified-ops, call/prototype specs, variable model, value+type facts}. This collapses A.S4/S5/S6 (and rejects B's forced S2/S3/S4 split and C's fictional S3-S6 order) into one stage that owns FOUR co-resident artifacts, each with substages: (i) call/prototype specs (A.S4), (ii) value+type facts (A.S5, but split the range-facts substage out and give it an edge to S3 jump-table bounds), (iii) variable/storage model (A.S6). Mark the schedule (Ghidra interleaved-in-mainloop vs angr/Reko post-stabilization solver) as a documented substage property per C's cross-cutting finding.
- S7 Structured Region Tree (A.S7) - sblocks (funcdata.hh:95), distinct from S3's bblocks. Keep separate; this is the second strongest verified split.
- S8 Token Stream & Rendered Text (A.S8) - naming, casts (cast.cc reads TypeFactory but emits late), formats.

SUB-STAGE CATALOGS TO KEEP: take B's catalog wholesale - every substage carries (assertion_type, lock_strength HARD|HINT, re_run_scope, LATENT?). Keep B's LATENT flagging (range-granularity threshold 4, maxpass budget, per-variable explicit/implied, solver pass-cap 7, Ghidra-has-no-goto-rollback) as the kuna product roadmap. Keep A's substage decisions where they are finer (SSA property-toggle, deadcode-delay).

FEEDBACK EDGE MODEL: edges are 'stage X invalidates artifact of stage Y' (A/H4), but EACH EDGE additionally carries C's two attributes: (1) rewind_scope in {op, block, region, function, program} and (2) survivability = what persists the rewind (the durable assertion). Mechanism types: keep A's a-e but add C's distinction restart-clear-replay vs reduced-pipeline-sub-query (stageJumpTable) as a sub-type of (c), and represent B's worklist-re-enqueue and lazy-dirty-recompute as edge ANNOTATIONS, not new top-level types (they are scheduling details, not new feedback semantics). Make the edge graph the literal re-run dependency graph so kuna can compute a scoped re-run (angr reflow-style: type-lock -> re-run B1.types + S8 only) instead of Ghidra's full clearAnalysis.

STRADDLER REGISTRY: add an explicit list of multi-artifact Actions (ActionDeadCode, jumptable recover, ActionInferTypes-in-mainloop) recording home-artifact + secondary-effect edges, so the placement-test promise ('locate any file in exactly one stage') is honestly qualified rather than silently violated.
